name: SZA
label: Top Dawg Entertainment / RCA
lede: A marine biology dropout who built her first EP on beats she found online, then made fans wait five years for the follow-up to Ctrl. When SOS finally arrived, Pitchfork put it at No. 1 for 2023.

eras.title: She was going to study fish
eras.text: Solána Rowe grew up in New Jersey and studied marine biology. A friend passed a few of her songs to the right person at Top Dawg Entertainment, and the science career stopped mattering.

years.h: Born in St. Louis, raised in Maplewood, New Jersey
years.p: Solána Imani Rowe's mother was an AT&T executive and her father a CNN video producer. She went to Sunday school and Muslim school both.

years.h: One semester short of a marine biology degree
years.p: SZA left Delaware State University in her final semester, then paid rent by bartending and dancing.
years.xp: The stage name came later. According to Wikipedia, SZA comes from the Supreme Alphabet of the Five Percent Nation: S for savior or sovereign, Z for Zig-Zag, A for Allah. It also happens to sit next to RZA and GZA of [[Wu-Tang Clan|0febdcf7-4e1f-4661-9493-b40427de2c13]].

years.h: A clothing brand, a Kendrick Lamar show and a friend with a demo
years.p: At CMJ 2011 her boyfriend's clothing company sponsored a show featuring [[Kendrick Lamar|381086ea-f511-4aba-bdf9-71c753dc5077]]. A friend passed her tracks to TDE president Terrence "Punch" Henderson.
years.xp: Nothing was signed that night. Per Wikipedia's account, Punch liked what he heard, kept in touch, and signed her to TDE two years later.

years.h: See.SZA.Run runs on beats borrowed from the internet
years.p: She self-released the 24-minute EP, made with a neighbor and, in her words, beats taken off the internet.
years.xp:
SZA has said she recorded it with a nearby friend using production apps and internet beats, with no plan for it to become a career. Producers credited include brandUn DeShay and AP Super, and working with DeShay led to more formal collaborations.

Complex called it made for multiple listens. The Guardian's Paul Lester compared her to Drake, the Weeknd, Miguel and Frank Ocean, calling her "the female version" of them.

years.cap: SZA on stage in Toronto, August 2013
years.h: Top Dawg signs SZA, the label's first woman
years.p: She joins a roster that already includes Lamar and [[Schoolboy Q|bce6d667-cde8-485e-b078-c0a05adea36d]], two years after Punch first heard her tracks.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the signing to July 14, 2013. Her second EP, S, had come out that April, three months earlier.

eras.title: Z, then the long wait
eras.text: She put out a ten-song TDE debut and wrote songs for bigger names. The first album was promised for 2015 and didn't show up.

years.h: Z brings Kendrick and Chance the Rapper along
years.p: Ten songs, produced in part by [[Mac Miller|a0e8a1b1-5f8f-475a-a253-17415c17d0ff]], Emile Haynie and Toro y Moi. Pitchfork gave it 5.9.
years.xp:
"Babylon" with Lamar was the lead single, its video set in swampy baptismal waters. Chance the Rapper guests on "Child's Play" and TDE labelmate [[Isaiah Rashad|37547347-ea75-45fa-9766-ff36b44d8147]] on "Warm Winds".

Wikipedia reports it debuted at No. 39 on the Billboard 200 with 6,980 copies and had sold more than 26,000 in the US in total. Metacritic averaged 66 from 15 reviews.

years.cap: SZA at the Pitchfork Music Festival, Chicago, July 18, 2014
years.h: She co-writes Nicki Minaj and Beyoncé's "Feeling Myself"
years.p: Wikipedia dates the co-write to 2014. It was the first of several songs she wrote for bigger names while her own record waited.

years.h: The album due in late 2015 is not due in late 2015
years.p: Ctrl was announced for the end of 2015, then for early 2016, and missed both.
years.xp: She co-wrote "Ok Alright" for [[Travis Scott|e4a51f17-a57b-47b1-b37b-f552d0f8e9e6]] in 2015 during the wait. Ctrl itself was recorded from 2014 to 2017, across multiple studios.

years.h: "LouAnne Johnson" was hers until it became Rihanna's "Consideration"
years.p: The song began as a SZA track meant for Ctrl. TDE reassigned it to [[Rihanna|73e5e69d-3554-40d8-8516-00cb38737a1c]]'s album Anti.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists it among her 2016 songwriting credits, alongside the earlier co-writes with Beyoncé and Minaj. It is the one that started life as her own.

eras.title: Ctrl takes over the charts
eras.text: Three years after Z, Ctrl debuted at No. 3 and stayed on the chart for years. A Black Panther single followed, then Grammy nominations.

years.h: "Drew Barrymore" opens Ctrl, and the actual Drew Barrymore shows up
years.p: The first single from Ctrl comes with a video that features the actress herself.

years.big: A kind of blinding paralysis brought on by anxiety
years.h: The label takes her hard drive
years.p: That is SZA's stated reason, per Wikipedia, for years of delays. In spring 2017 her label confiscated her hard drive to finish the album from roughly 150 to 200 recorded tracks.
years.xp: Wikipedia also notes that she signed with RCA Records in April 2017, two months before release.

yt: Love Galore ft. Travis Scott, official video
years.h: Ctrl opens at No. 3 and will not leave the chart
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.4. It opened with 60,000 units and by February 2025 had logged 400 weeks on the Billboard 200.
years.xp:
Guests include Lamar on "Doves in the Wind", Scott on "Love Galore" and Rashad on "Pretty Little Birds". Producers include Carter Lang, ThankGod4Cody, Scum and Craig Balmoris. Metacritic averaged 87 from 17 reviews.

Time put it at the top of its year-end ranking, per Wikipedia. It is the second longest-charting R&B album by a woman.

years.cap: SZA on the Ctrl Tour, Toronto
years.h: "All the Stars" with Lamar, for Black Panther
years.p: The lead single of the soundtrack Ryan Coogler asked Lamar to produce. It peaked at No. 7 on the Hot 100.
years.xp:
It earned four Grammy nominations, including Record of the Year and Song of the Year, plus Oscar and Golden Globe nominations for Best Original Song. Reviews split: Rolling Stone's Jon Blistein called SZA's vocal "enthralling" and Pitchfork's Sheldon Pearce called the song "generic".

The video, from Dave Meyers and the Little Homies, has passed 583 million YouTube views as of September 2025, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Five Grammy nominations, including Best New Artist, and no wins
years.p: Ctrl's Best Urban Contemporary Album nod was one of them. The 60th Grammys sent her home empty-handed.

eras.title: Free SZA
eras.text: SOS was announced as imminent in 2019 and arrived in December 2022. In between came a fan hashtag, a public wobble with the label, and a Grammy for a pop duet.

years.h: SOS is coming "soon as fuck"
years.p: That was SZA's own promise in August 2019. The album came out three years and four months later.

years.big: At this point y'all gotta ask Punch.
years.h: #FreeSZA, and a tweet about the boss
years.p: SZA tweeted this, per Wikipedia, then deleted it, while fans campaigned for the album under #FreeSZA.
years.xp:
She followed up by saying Punch had only ever told her "soon" about release dates. Wikipedia says she later revealed that her relationship with her label had been hostile since the delays.

She also pushed back on the hashtag itself: she wasn't being held hostage, she said, and "sometimes no is a blessing."

years.h: "Good Days" lands on Christmas Day and reaches No. 9
years.p: It was her first top 10 as a lead artist on the Hot 100.
years.xp:
She started it on producer Carter Lang's birthday, December 11, 2018, and "finished it randomly" in 2020. [[Jacob Collier|1df15ee0-b52b-4315-9cb9-bc5a27a685e9]] co-wrote it and cameos in the video, which SZA directed, as the man in the green television.

Pitchfork ranked it No. 20 on its 100 best songs of 2021.

years.h: "Kiss Me More" with Doja Cat wins her first Grammy
years.p: The Planet Her lead single reached No. 3 on the Hot 100. At the 2022 Grammys it won Best Pop Duo/Group Performance, the first win for both artists.
years.xp: It interpolates the melody of Olivia Newton-John's "Physical", so Steve Kipner and Terry Shaddick share songwriting credit. Warren Fu directed the video, which puts both singers on a planet of aliens.

years.h: A yacht, a St. Louis Blues jersey and Princess Diana
years.p: SZA wears a modified Blues jersey in a shot that references a Princess Diana photo from Portofino, Italy.
years.xp: "I pulled the Diana reference because I just loved how isolated she felt," SZA said. Art director Jass Bell designed the jersey.

years.cap: SZA in a video call, May 2022
years.src: SOS (SZA album) - Wikipedia · SZA - SOS - Reviews - Album of The Year
years.h: SOS has 23 tracks, three guest verses and an Ol' Dirty Bastard sample
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.7 and Best New Music. It opened at No. 1 with 318,000 units.
years.xp:
SZA asked around for features and got verses from only three people: [[Don Toliver|a0723a3c-4135-438e-85c5-012712144ede]], [[Phoebe Bridgers|96855c21-b832-4366-ba12-0d2330c36a86]] and Scott. Producers include Babyface, Benny Blanco, Rodney Jerkins and DJ Dahi, with ThankGod4Cody co-producing seven tracks. It samples the late Ol' Dirty Bastard.

Metacritic averaged 90 from 20 reviews. The Observer, at 60, was the outlier, finding a fine line between versatility and no cohesion.

eras.title: The year SOS wouldn't leave
eras.text: An album from the previous December became the story of 2023: a video, a tour, a No. 1 single and Pitchfork's top spot.

years.src: Kill Bill (song) - Wikipedia · SOS (SZA album) - Wikipedia
years.h: "Kill Bill" gets a video with Vivica A. Fox in it
years.p: Christian Breslauer directed. Fox, who starred in the Tarantino films the song is named for, has a cameo.
years.xp: Breslauer said of Quentin Tarantino, "Tarantino is the ultimate chop and screw hybrid filmmaker in how he grabs from so many films and genres." The song gave SZA her first No. 1 on the Hot 100 and later spent 21 weeks at No. 1 on Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs, per Wikipedia.

years.h: The SOS Tour runs 15 months
years.p: It started in February 2023 and ended in May 2024. Omar Apollo opened, and Raye joined for the European dates.

years.h: "Snooze" charts all 52 weeks of 2023
years.p: It became a single on April 25 and later won Best R&B Song at the 2024 Grammys.

years.src: Pitchfork: The 50 Best Albums of 2023 - Year-End Lists · SOS (SZA album) - Wikipedia · SZA - SOS - Reviews - Album of The Year
years.h: Pitchfork puts SOS at No. 1, ahead of Caroline Polachek
years.p: Its 8.7 had already tagged it Best New Music. [[Caroline Polachek|d8f43dc5-4613-48ac-8c23-a62b82f8c67a]] took second and [[Billy Woods|f30fea51-fa9c-4067-bc49-fc43236e89ba]] with Kenny Segal third.
years.xp:
Pitchfork's list has SOS at 1, Desire, I Want to Turn Into You at 2, Maps at 3, Wednesday's Rat Saw God at 4 and Nourished by Time's Erotic Probiotic 2 at 5. Wikipedia adds that Rolling Stone, the Los Angeles Times and the Philadelphia Inquirer also put it first.

Album of the Year averages 25 critic scores at 85, with NME and The Telegraph at 100 and The Observer at 60.

eras.title: Lana, Luther and the stadium tour
eras.text: Nine Grammy nominations for SOS, a deluxe reissue, a Super Bowl halftime slot and a tour with Kendrick Lamar that outsold every rap tour before it.

years.src: SOS (SZA album) - Wikipedia · Kill Bill (song) - Wikipedia
years.h: Nine Grammy nominations for SOS, one win
years.p: It lost Album of the Year to Taylor Swift's Midnights and won Best Progressive R&B Album.
years.xp: "Kill Bill" was nominated for Record of the Year, Song of the Year and Best R&B Performance, per Wikipedia. Rolling Stone later put it at No. 267 on its 500 greatest songs.

years.h: "Luther" with Lamar debuts at No. 3, then stays No. 1 for 13 weeks
years.p: It came off Lamar's GNX on November 29 and reached the top on March 1, 2025.
years.xp: At the 68th Grammys it won Record of the Year and Best Melodic Rap Performance, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Lana adds 15 songs to SOS
years.p: The deluxe reissue includes "Saturn" and "Drive" and sends SOS back to No. 1 in 2025.
years.xp: A further reissue on February 9, 2025 added four more tracks, per Wikipedia.

yt: Super Bowl halftime with Kendrick Lamar
years.h: SZA joins Lamar at the Super Bowl LIX halftime show
years.p: They performed "Luther" live for the first time there.

years.cap: SZA and Kendrick Lamar on the Grand National Tour, July 23, 2025
years.h: Grand National Tour: 47 shows, $390.7 million
years.p: Wikipedia lists it as the highest-earning rap tour ever. SZA played the North American and European dates.
years.xp: Mustard opened, and 2.037 million tickets sold. SZA launched her makeup line, Not Beauty, through tour pop-ups and posted behind-the-scenes vlogs from the road.
